instruction: Switch the desktop clock to 12-hour format.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully turned volume to max by opening GNOME quick settings panel via system tray click and dragging volume slider to the right. Completed in 4 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open GNOME system tray quick settings, interact with volume slider, click UI elements in the panel
metadata.task_rationale: Tests a different system setting accessible through the Settings app. The model showed it can open quick settings where the Settings shortcut is visible. This variation requires navigating into GNOME Settings to change clock format.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the desktop clock to 12-hour format. Evaluator checks gsettings clock-format value. The model must navigate to GNOME Settings > Date & Time or use the quick settings Settings shortcut.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface clock-format' to check the GNOME clock format setting, which is the canonical way to verify this on GNOME desktops.
Expected value "'12h'\n" correctly matches the gsettings output format (single-quoted string with trailing newline).

Metric 'exact_match' receives the rules dict from get_rule, accesses rules['expected'] to get "'12h'\n", and performs exact string comparison against the getter output — this is correct and sufficient.
Full instruction coverage: the single requirement (switch to 12-hour format) is fully verified by checking the gsettings key.
No UI state dependency — gsettings is a persistent backend setting, so no postconfig is needed to read it.
